thread.title: Facebook’s ‘powerful’ ad business means it’s time to buy — analysts react to earnings

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Facebook’s ‘powerful’ ad business means it’s time to buy — analysts react to earnings
text:
Facebook Inc. and its plump profit margins continue to please investors and analysts, despite the company’s massive investments in infrastructure spending, tax charges and big bets on improving its users’ experience by tinkering with its news feed cash cow.
Following a fourth-quarter earnings report released Wednesday , 21 analysts upped price targets Thursday, setting the new average at $220.32, reflecting 14% upside from Thursday’s intraday price of $193.03, up 3.3% on the day. Immediately following Wednesday’s results, investors sent the stock plunging after quarterly figures showed a drop in time spent by users on the platform.
The company’s ad pricing showed massive growth, however, and turned the stock around . 
“Strong demand from advertisers drove average ad pricing up 42%,” KeyBanc Capital Markets analysts, led by Andy Hargreaves, remarked in a note.
Facebook’s earnings reveal “a very powerful ad platform,” the KeyBanc analysts also said, as they backed their buy rating and raised their price target to $245 from $220, implying a rally of 31% from the stock’s closing price Wednesday of about $187.
The ad platform’s growth is coming from Facebook’s increasingly strong ad targeting and its ability to demonstrate a return on investment to advertisers using the platform, Barclays analyst Ross Sandler wrote in a Thursday note to clients. Improvements to the ad tech drive up competition in auctions for ad space, which in turn results in a higher price per ad.
“[This] is a trend we see continuing for the foreseeable future,” he wrote. Sandler has a $225 price target with the equivalent of a buy rating on the name.
Even though earnings were hit by a tax charge —which appears similar to what other companies have announced —analysts such as Baird’s Colin Sebastian noted that the company’s operating margins improved due to superior cost controls on expenses such as research and development, as well as sales and marketing. Sebastian rates Facebook a buy with a $225 price target. 

Read: The YouTube and Instagram secret that Google and Facebook don’t want you to know 
Heading into earnings, investors wondered how big changes to Facebook’s news feed would affect results. CEO Mark Zuckerberg addressed the effects of some changes, saying users were spending fewer hours a day on the platform, a MarketWatch story noted .
Facebook bulls sounded placated by the company’s explanations.
Management “said news feed changes to promote meaningful interaction would likely not negatively impact ad rev growth. That’s our POV, too,” said RBC Capital Markets analyst led by Mark Mahaney. POV stands for point of view.
The RBC team hiked its price target to $250 from $230 and reiterated its outperform rating.
Barclays’ Sandler said that executives “did a solid job of addressing the growing ‘Facebook is bad for society’ narrative on the call,” but cautioned that regulatory and media scrutiny will continue through 2018.
The changes Facebook executives have promised, especially in regards to tightening up its security procedures that keep offensive content off its platform, will cost the company hundreds of millions of dollars a year though.

“We estimate that the new dedicated safety and security head count alone will increase operating expense by $1.5 billion in 2018,” Wedbush analyst Michael Pachter wrote in a note to clients, adding that Facebook executives have adequately included the team’s estimate within its operating expenses guidance. Pachter has the equivalent of a buy on the stock with a $260 price target.
In regards to Facebook’s projected operational expenditures—which executives have guided for $7 billion in 2018—Pachter said that he doesn’t believe the company will be able to actually figure out enough new projects.
“We are skeptical that the company can actually find that many projects to fund,” Pachter wrote. “We have modeled spending growth at the low end of the guidance range, but believe that our estimate may prove to be too high.”
Facebook is one of six companies that have topped a $500 billion market valuation and are reporting results Wednesday and Thursday (the others are Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. BABA, -5.91% Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, -0.05% GOOG, -0.19% , Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -4.20% Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.21% and Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -0.79% ).

Of the 46 analysts that cover Facebook, 42 rate the stock the equivalent of a buy, three rate it a hold and two have a sell recommendation, according to FactSet. Facebook stock has gained 46% in the past 12 months, with the S&P 500 index SPX, -0.06% rising 24%.
